blocks.title: Air Quality Index
blocks.text: Air quality is measured by the Air Quality Index (AQI), a measure of the concentrations of pollutants in the air at a particular location. When air quality is good the air is clear and contains only small amounts of solid particles and chemical pollutants; poor air quality, with high levels, is often hazy and dangerous to health and the environment.

An AQI value under 50 is considered good: it is safe to spend time outdoors without risk to health. An AQI over 300 is hazardous. Children under 18, adults over 65 and people with chronic heart and lung disease are at high risk, and outdoor workers are at higher risk because of prolonged exposure.
